analysis: The dense-convolution candidate completed all 30 epochs, with its best checkpoint at epoch 10. Validation HR@10 reached 0.615, improving on the preceding 0.605 by 0.010 but remaining 0.010 below the recorded best of 0.625. This supports dense temporal convolutions as a useful candidate under the frozen protocol, but does not establish that cross-channel connectivity caused the improvement or improves generalization. Retain the 0.625 checkpoint as the best available.
code_summary: Changed both temporal convolutions in each NextItNetBlock from depthwise groups=hidden_units to dense groups=1. Preserved eight independent 64-channel residual blocks, dilation schedule [1,2,1,2,1,2,1,2], kernel size 3, left-only causal padding, and the 49-position receptive field. Retained pointwise mixing, sigmoid gating, GELU, LayerNorm, dropout 0.2, padding masks, item and positional embeddings, tied item scoring, last-nonpadding candidate selection, all interfaces, and all constants. Training and evaluation remain host-owned.
